code.title: Word Length Reporter
code.description:
A text tool reports statistics about a single word. Read one word (a single token with no spaces) and print the word together with its length.

Input Format:
One line with one word.

Output Format:
Word: <word>
Length: <number of characters>

Constraints:
1 <= word length <= 100

code.title: Shout It in Capitals
code.description:
A notification banner must be loud. Read one word and print it converted to all uppercase letters. Lowercase letters become uppercase; other characters stay unchanged.

Input Format:
One line with one word.

Output Format:
Loud: <uppercase word>

Constraints:
1 <= word length <= 100, word contains letters and digits only
code.inputconstrains: 1 <= word length <= 100, letters and digits only

code.title: Vowel Counter Drill
code.description:
A spelling coach counts vowels. Read one word and print how many vowels it contains. Both lowercase and uppercase vowels count (a, e, i, o, u).

Input Format:
One line with one word.

Output Format:
Vowels: <count>

Constraints:
1 <= word length <= 100, word contains English letters only

code.title: Word Reverse Drill
code.description:
A palindrome training app first shows a word backwards. Read one word and print it reversed (last character first).

Input Format:
One line with one word.

Output Format:
Reversed: <reversed word>

Constraints:
1 <= word length <= 100

code.title: Name Badge Character Count
code.description:
A badge printer reads the visitor's full name, which may contain spaces. Read the whole line with getline and print the total number of characters (spaces included) and the first character.

Input Format:
One line containing the full name (may contain spaces, at least one character).

Output Format:
Name: <name>
Characters: <length including spaces>
First letter: <first character>

Constraints:
1 <= name length <= 50

Name: Linus
Characters: 5
First letter: L

Name: Alan Turing
Characters: 11
First letter: A
code.output3:
Name: M
Characters: 1
First letter: M

Name: Ada Lovelace
Characters: 12
First letter: A
code.sampleoutput2:
Name: Grace Hopper
Characters: 12
First letter: G

code.title: Two Words in Dictionary Order
code.description:
A sorting drill teaches dictionary (lexicographic) order, where comparison follows character codes, so capitals come before lowercase. Read two different words and print the one that comes first in dictionary order, then the other one.

Input Format:
One line with two different words separated by a space.

Output Format:
First line: the word that comes earlier in dictionary order
Second line: the other word

Constraints:
1 <= each word length <= 20, the two words are different
code.inputconstrains: 1 <= each word length <= 20, words are different

code.title: Username Validator Lite
code.description:
A signup screen performs a quick username check before calling the server. Read the username (a single word) and validate it in this order: if its length is less than 5 it is rejected as too short; else if its length is greater than 15 it is rejected as too long; else if it does not start with an English letter it is rejected; otherwise it is accepted.

Input Format:
One line with one word: the username.

Output Format:
Exactly one line:
Valid username
or
Invalid: too short
or
Invalid: too long
or
Invalid: must start with a letter

Constraints:
1 <= username length <= 50, username contains letters, digits and underscores
code.output2: Invalid: must start with a letter

code.title: SKU Code Formatter
code.description:
A catalogue system formats product codes by attaching the code length. Read the product code (a single word) and print it followed by a dash and its length.

Input Format:
One line with one word: the product code.

Output Format:
Code: <code>-<length>

Constraints:
1 <= code length <= 30

code.title: Greeting Composer
code.description:
A mail-merge tool composes greetings. Read a person's first name and last name (two words) and print a greeting plus the initials built from the first character of each name.

Input Format:
One line with two words: first name and last name.

Output Format:
Hello, <first> <last>!
Initials: <F>.<L>.

Constraints:
1 <= each name length <= 20
code.subtopic: C-Style Strings and the string Class

code.title: PIN Strength Label
code.description:
A banking app labels PIN strength by length only. Read the PIN as a digit string and print its length and the label: WEAK when the length is less than 4, MEDIUM when the length is 4 to 6, STRONG when the length is greater than 6.

Input Format:
One line with one digit string (characters '0' to '9' only).

Output Format:
PIN length: <length>
Strength: <WEAK or MEDIUM or STRONG>

Constraints:
1 <= PIN length <= 20

code.title: Case-Blind Palindrome Checker
code.description:
A quality team checks product tags that must read the same forwards and backwards, ignoring letter case. Read one word, compare it with its reverse case-insensitively, and print the verdict.

Input Format:
One line with one word (English letters only).

Output Format:
Palindrome
or
Not a palindrome

Constraints:
1 <= word length <= 100

code.title: Anagram Pair Checker
code.description:
A puzzle app checks whether two words use exactly the same letters with the same counts, ignoring case. Read two words and print whether they are anagrams.

Input Format:
One line with two words separated by a space (English letters only).

Output Format:
Anagrams
or
Not anagrams

Constraints:
1 <= each word length <= 100
code.inputconstrains: 1 <= each word length <= 100, English letters only

code.title: Word Frequency Counter
code.description:
A content moderator counts how many times a given word appears in a comment line, matching case-insensitively and only as a whole word. Read the target word, then read the whole comment line with getline, and print how many whole-word matches exist.

Input Format:
Line 1: the target word (single token).
Line 2: the comment sentence (words separated by single spaces).

Output Format:
Count: <number of case-insensitive whole-word matches>

Constraints:
1 <= target word length <= 20, 1 <= sentence length <= 200, sentence words contain letters only
code.sampleinput1:
cat
The cat sat on the mat with another CAT
code.sampleinput2:
code
Coding is fun because code makes CODE work
code.input1:
a
a A a banana a
code.input2:
data
Big data needs clean data and DATA

code.title: Run-Length Text Compressor
code.description:
A log shipper shrinks text by replacing each run of repeated letters with the letter followed by the run length. Read one lowercase word and print its compressed form. Example: aaabb becomes a3b2 and a single letter becomes a1.

Input Format:
One line with one word of lowercase letters.

Output Format:
Compressed: <compressed form>

Constraints:
1 <= word length <= 60

code.title: Case Toggle Transformer
code.description:
A chat app has a playful toggle mode that flips the case of every letter: lowercase becomes uppercase and uppercase becomes lowercase. Read one word and print the flipped version. Non-letter characters stay unchanged.

Input Format:
One line with one word (letters and digits).

Output Format:
Toggled: <flipped word>

Constraints:
1 <= word length <= 100
code.inputconstrains: 1 <= word length <= 100, letters and digits only

code.title: Digit Digger Sum Report
code.description:
A warehouse scanner reads messy storage labels that mix letters and digits. Read the label as one word, print the sequence of all digit characters in order, and print their sum. If the label has no digits, print none for the digit sequence.

Input Format:
One line with one word (letters and digits only).

Output Format:
Digits: <digits in order, or none>
Sum: <sum of the digit values>

Constraints:
1 <= label length <= 100
code.inputconstrains: 1 <= label length <= 100, letters and digits only

code.title: License Plate Rule Engine
code.description:
A regional transport office validates license plate codes with five rules, checked on the plate string:
- Rule 1: length must be between 6 and 10 characters inclusive
- Rule 2: every character must be an English letter or a digit (no symbols like - or _)
- Rule 3: the plate must contain at least one digit
- Rule 4: the plate must contain at least one letter
- Rule 5: the sum of all digit characters must be divisible by 7
Print each rule as PASS or FAIL, then the overall verdict: VALID only when every rule passes.

Input Format:
One line with one plate code (a single token).

Output Format:
Rule 1 (length 6-10): PASS or FAIL
Rule 2 (letters and digits only): PASS or FAIL
Rule 3 (has a digit): PASS or FAIL
Rule 4 (has a letter): PASS or FAIL
Rule 5 (digit sum divisible by 7): PASS or FAIL
Verdict: VALID or INVALID

Constraints:
1 <= plate length <= 20
code.output1:
Rule 1 (length 6-10): PASS
Rule 2 (letters and digits only): PASS
Rule 3 (has a digit): PASS
Rule 4 (has a letter): FAIL
Rule 5 (digit sum divisible by 7): PASS
Verdict: INVALID
code.output2:
Rule 1 (length 6-10): PASS
Rule 2 (letters and digits only): PASS
Rule 3 (has a digit): PASS
Rule 4 (has a letter): PASS
Rule 5 (digit sum divisible by 7): FAIL
Verdict: INVALID
code.output3:
Rule 1 (length 6-10): PASS
Rule 2 (letters and digits only): PASS
Rule 3 (has a digit): PASS
Rule 4 (has a letter): PASS
Rule 5 (digit sum divisible by 7): PASS
Verdict: VALID
code.sampleoutput1:
Rule 1 (length 6-10): PASS
Rule 2 (letters and digits only): PASS
Rule 3 (has a digit): PASS

Rule 5 (digit sum divisible by 7): FAIL
Verdict: INVALID

code.title: Sentence Statistician
code.description:
An editor plugin analyzes a sentence and reports word statistics. Read the whole line with getline. Words are separated by one or more spaces. Print the number of words, the longest word, the shortest word and the average word length with exactly two decimals. If several words tie for longest or shortest, report the earliest one.

Input Format:
One line containing a sentence with at least one word.

Output Format:
Words: <count>
Longest: <longest word>
Shortest: <shortest word>
Average: <average word length with 2 decimals>

Constraints:
1 <= sentence length <= 300, words are separated by one or more spaces

Average: 1.00

Shortest: is

code.title: CSV Record Formatter
code.description:
A legacy HR export stores one record per line as name,department,score with exactly two commas. Read the whole line with getline, split it manually on the commas (no split libraries), and print the three parsed fields, followed by a padded table row: the name padded with trailing spaces to width 10, the department padded to width 12, and the score right-aligned in width 5, all between | characters.

Input Format:
One line: name,department,score (name and department contain no commas; score is an integer).

Output Format:
Name: <name>
Department: <dept>
Score: <score>
Row: |<name width 10>|<dept width 12>|<score width 5 right-aligned>|

Constraints:
1 <= name length <= 10, 1 <= department length <= 12, 0 <= score <= 100

code.title: Caesar Cipher Engine
code.description:
A secret club encodes messages with a Caesar cipher. Read a word and a shift K. Shift every letter forward by K positions in the alphabet, wrapping around from z to a (and Z to A) while preserving case. Print the plain word, the cipher text, and the cipher text reversed.

Input Format:
One line with a word (English letters only) and an integer K separated by a space.

Output Format:
Plain: <word>
Cipher: <shifted word>
Backwards: <reversed cipher>

Constraints:
1 <= word length <= 50, 0 <= K <= 25
code.output1:
Plain: wrap
Cipher: gbkz
Backwards: zkbg
code.output2:
Plain: XYZ
Cipher: CDE
Backwards: EDC
code.output3:
Plain: cipher
Cipher: bhogdq
Backwards: qdgohb
code.sampleoutput1:

Cipher: dwwdfn
Backwards: nfdwwd
code.sampleoutput2:

Backwards: bscfA
